solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Nomadic Romanies overwhelming outwardly idyllic archipelago

indicators.note: one piece overwhelms another by closing round it, so the shuffled letters surround the next piece
nomads wander about, so the letters of the word Romanies roam into a new order
outwardly means only the outside letters of the word idyllic are used

explanation.surface: Travelling Romany people take over an idyllic group of islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nomadic' makes MRONESIA, which 'overwhelming' wraps round the edges taken by 'outwardly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Micronesia is a group of small Pacific islands, an example of an archipelago.

clue.text: One encroaches upon rocky ravine when touring Germany

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the jumbled letters go round the next piece
rocky suggests something shaky or unstable, so the letters of ravine are jumbled

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)

explanation.surface: An intruder pushes into a craggy gorge while travelling through Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocky' rearranges RAVINE to INVAER, and 'touring' puts it round D.
explanation.definitionFit: An invader is someone who trespasses or intrudes on another's territory.

clue.text: Frenchwoman born alongside banks of Rhone

indicators.note: alongside means the two pieces sit next to each other
the banks of a river are its two edges, so the first and last letters of the word Rhone are taken

parts.note: née is used before a woman's maiden name, meaning born

explanation.surface: A French woman was born beside the Rhone river.
explanation.definitionFit: Renée is a common French female first name, so it stands for a Frenchwoman.

clue.text: Flower sad in shade

parts.note: a 'flower' in crosswords is something that flows, a river: the Nile
feeling blue means feeling sad

explanation.surface: A wilting bloom droops in the shadow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' wants to be a bloom; it is a river, the thing that flows.
explanation.definitionFit: Nile blue is a pale greenish-blue colour, and a shade is a colour variant.

clue.text: Old golfer assimilated bestseller with Soave

indicators.note: assimilated means absorbed and blended together, so the letters of the two words are mixed into one new string

explanation.surface: A retired golfer has digested a popular book along with a glass of Italian white wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Soave is an Italian white wine, which helps the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish player who won five majors and died in 2011 is a golfer of the past.

clue.text: Donkey starts to untie cheap harness by itself

parts.note: an ass is a donkey

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, here of untie, cheap and harness

explanation.surface: A donkey begins to free itself from a cheap harness on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in itself or intrinsically, considered on its own terms.

clue.text: Impersonate policeman and end in custody

parts.note: a cop is a policeman

indicators.note: end in means the final letter of the word custody

explanation.surface: Someone poses as a police officer and finishes up locked up.
explanation.definitionFit: To copy someone is to imitate or mimic them, which is what impersonating means.

clue.text: Herb, fellow jockey, pens article

indicators.note: pens means encloses, so the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: a fellow jockey is a co-rider in the same race
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A herb and a fellow jockey write an article together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pens' looks like writing but means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: Coriander is a leafy plant used as a culinary herb and spice.

clue.text: Rustic game-bird husband picked off

indicators.note: picked off means removed, so one letter is taken out of the bird

parts.note: a pheasant is a game bird

explanation.surface: A countryman shoots a game bird, and its owner is picked off too.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustic is a country person, a farm worker of humble rural life.

clue.text: Recalled star GB runner

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a nova is a star that suddenly brightens

explanation.surface: A British athletics star is brought back to the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' looks like an athlete but means a river: the Avon is a river in England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Avon is a British river, and rivers are crossword runners.

clue.text: Irishman describes underwear on broadcast online

indicators.note: describes in the sense of drawing around, so the name goes round the other pieces

parts.note: Liam is a typical Irish man's name
a vest is a piece of underwear
re means on, concerning

explanation.surface: An Irishman talks about his underwear on an internet broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describes' is used in its geometric sense of tracing a line around.
explanation.definitionFit: To livestream is to transmit video over the internet as it happens.

clue.text: A level of noise inhibits vicar going over part of speech

indicators.note: inhibits means holds in, so the first piece keeps the second inside

parts.note: dB, the decibel, is a measure of sound level

indicators.note: going over suggests turning over, so the word is reversed

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a vicar's title

explanation.surface: Some noise holds back a priest as he crosses to make a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going over' gives VER, which 'inhibits' puts inside the decibel symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverb is a word class, one of the grammatical categories of language.

clue.text: Current coach seen in club's card game

indicators.note: seen in means the pieces appear inside the next word

parts.note: a bat is a club used in games
AC is alternating current
a car is a railway coach

explanation.surface: A trendy coach is spotted playing cards at the club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like up-to-date but means electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: Baccarat is a gambling game played with cards, popular in casinos.

clue.text: Composed new design to reflect trimmed bedcover

indicators.note: a reflection reverses an image, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: art is design or creative skill

indicators.note: trimmed means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a quilt is a bedcover

explanation.surface: A calm designer makes a new pattern to mirror a shortened duvet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reflect' turns NART into TRAN; 'trimmed' cuts QUILT to QUIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Composed here is the adjective meaning calm and unruffled, a synonym.

clue.text: Former politician Rob — Conservative member, note

parts.note: to nick is to steal or rob
a leg is a limb or member
G is a musical note

explanation.surface: An ex-politician robs a Tory MP and leaves a note.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick Clegg led the UK Liberal Democrats and was Deputy Prime Minister 2010-15.
explanation.definitionFit: He was a British Deputy Prime Minister and party leader who has left politics.

clue.text: Spot first of hinds and does earlier

parts.note: a dot is a spot

indicators.note: first of means just the opening letter of the word hinds

explanation.surface: Spot the leading female deer, and then the other female deer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'does' looks like female deer, matching hinds; it is the verb, in an older form.
explanation.definitionFit: Doth is the archaic third person singular of do, used in earlier English.

clue.text: Small daughters inside ground later sit on the fence

indicators.note: inside means the next piece is put within the rearranged letters
ground means crushed and broken up, so the letters of the word later are rearranged

parts.note: D is daughter, so DD is daughters

explanation.surface: Little girls inside the grounds later sit on a fence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' makes TRALE, and 'inside' puts the two daughters within it.
explanation.definitionFit: To straddle an issue is to avoid taking a side, an idiom for staying undecided.

clue.text: Element of jazz in composition

indicators.note: of here means taken from within, so the letters are found in the run of words jazz in composition

explanation.surface: A key ingredient of a jazz piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Element' looks like a component of the music; it is a chemical element.
explanation.definitionFit: Zinc is a metallic chemical element with atomic number 30.

clue.text: In Royal Crown, artist's drawn still life?

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for royalty

indicators.note: drawn means pulled out, so the letters go from the crown

parts.note: a tiara is a crown
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: An artist's painting of a still life hangs in the Royal Crown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawn' suggests painting but means withdrawn; 'still life' is a life without movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is a lazy lack of motion or activity, a life lived standing still.

clue.text: Cattle, leaderless between nine and eleven, run outside

indicators.note: leaderless means without its first letter

parts.note: Dexter is a small breed of Irish cattle
ten comes between nine and eleven, written as the digits 1 and 0, which look like the letters IO
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Leaderless cattle run outdoors between nine and eleven o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaderless' removes D from DEXTER; the number 10 is read as the letters I and O.
explanation.definitionFit: The outside of something is its exterior, the outer surface.

clue.text: Kind of top athlete to change policy about entrant in Marathon

indicators.note: about means going round, so the reordered letters go round the next piece
to change means the letters of the word policy are reordered
an entrant is what goes in first, so the opening letter of the word Marathon

explanation.surface: An elite runner changes policy about who can enter a marathon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' turns POLICY into OLYPIC and 'about' puts it round M.
explanation.definitionFit: An Olympic athlete competes at the highest level of international sport.

clue.text: Bubbly resident in middle of romcom that provides tackiness

indicators.note: resident in means living within, so the wine sits inside the other letters
middle of means the central letters of the word romcom

parts.note: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

explanation.surface: Fizz in the middle of a romantic comedy gives it a cheesy, tacky feel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tackiness' suggests poor taste; here it is stickiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Mastic is a resin or putty used as an adhesive, something sticky.

clue.text: Dealer paid to maintain ranch building

indicators.note: to maintain is to hold, so the first piece holds the second

parts.note: to meet a bill is to pay it, so met means paid

indicators.note: building suggests construction, so the letters of the word ranch are rearranged

explanation.surface: A trader is paid to keep up a farm building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'building' looks like a noun but is the anagram signal, making ERCHAN, which 'to maintain' holds.
explanation.definitionFit: A merchant is a trader who buys and sells goods, a dealer.

clue.text: Maybe Pacino's absorbing passage continually

indicators.note: absorbing means taking in, so the first piece takes the next inside

parts.note: Al Pacino is one example of an Al, and the apostrophe s gives Al's
a way is a passage or route

explanation.surface: Perhaps Al Pacino's character keeps soaking up the passage over and over.
explanation.definitionFit: Always and continually are synonyms meaning at all times, without stopping.

clue.text: Body part rejected, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the word is spoken and sounds the same as another

parts.note: waste is material thrown away or rejected

explanation.surface: A body part was rejected, so we hear.
explanation.definitionFit: The waist is the narrow middle section of the human torso.

clue.text: Cryptic setter embarrassed by constant approval by modish urbanites?

indicators.note: cryptic means obscured or encoded, so the letters of setter are scrambled

parts.note: C is a constant in maths and physics, such as the speed of light
an embarrassed person goes red

explanation.surface: A crossword setter is embarrassed by the steady approval of trendy city-dwellers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cryptic' looks like it describes the setter, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Street cred is the credibility or respect earned among fashionable young urban people.

clue.text: Observing game is pretty draining

indicators.note: draining means emptying, so only the outer letters of the word pretty remain

explanation.surface: A watching game is rather tiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pretty draining' reads as 'quite exhausting', but 'pretty' is emptied.
explanation.definitionFit: I spy is a children's guessing game based on spotting things.

clue.text: Work hard to arrest northern poisoner

indicators.note: to arrest means to hold, so the first piece holds the next

parts.note: to fag is British slang for toiling or working hard

explanation.surface: Police work hard to arrest a poisoner from the North.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poisoner' suggests a murderer; it is a snake's venomous tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: A snake's fang is what injects venom, so it is the thing that poisons.

clue.text: Leaves company's rental property with Charlie during Tuesday

parts.note: Co is company, plus the apostrophe s
a let is a rented property

indicators.note: during means C sits within the abbreviation for the day

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A firm's tenant moves out with Charlie on Tuesday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb (departs) but is the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Cos lettuce is a salad plant grown for its edible green leaves.
